title.description: Its name for people, such as `Claude accounts`.

description.description: What it is and what it keeps, in a sentence or two for people.

settings.description: A guatiao schema (JSON Schema, `type: object`) for the kind's settings. A credential is a property marked `writeOnly` and `x-sensitive`, and its key is the key in [`Credentials`]. A host renders its form from this.

key.description: The kind's text setting holding an absolute URL; absent when the harness fixes it.

default.description: The URL used when the setting is absent.

endpoints.description: The URLs the kind talks to, for the host's egress policy.

rotates.description: A renewal replaces a credential so that an older copy stops working. The host holds such an account exclusively. A kind whose rotation is unmeasured says `true`.

history_portable.description: The harness keeps its sessions where every account of this kind shares them, so a session started on one account resumes on another directly, with nothing moved. `false` does not say the conversation cannot follow the person: where each account has its own directory ([`state_dir`](Self::state_dir)) a host exports it from the first account's with [`export_session`](crate::AcpHarness::export_session) and imports it into the second's with [`import_session`](crate::AcpHarness::import_session), then resumes it there.

state_dir.description: The kind needs a private directory where the harness runs ([`AccountGrant::state_dir`]).

renews.description: [`renew`](crate::AccountProvider::renew) can renew it with no model turn.

notices.description: What using it weakens, shown when the account is added and logged at start.

provides.description: The standards an account of this kind provides, each an id of [`crate::standard`]: what it can be used as. Empty: only this harness takes it.

kinds.description: The kinds of account it makes and keeps. Each says which standards an account of it provides, whether it rotates its login, keeps files, and renews with no model turn.

produces.description: The kind of account it makes: one of the catalog's kinds.

inputs.description: A schema of what is asked before it runs (an email, an issuer); an empty object asks nothing.

steps.description: The steps it relays, in the order they can come: [`OPEN_URL`], [`USER_CODE`], [`ASK`], [`PASTE_CODE`].

remote.description: Whether it works through a spawner that is not local. A loopback callback needs the person's browser on the machine where the CLI runs, so it is `false` unless the CLI offers a code to paste or a device code.

logins.description: The ways to sign in. Each names the kind it produces, which is listed in `kinds`.

usage.description: The kinds whose accounts report their plan's usage through [`AccountProvider::usage`]: ids listed in `kinds`, or [`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN) when `local` is true. A kind not here answers `usage` with "not offered".

local.description: Whether the provider's program has a login of its own that the provider offers as an automatic account named [`LOCAL_ACCOUNT`](crate::LOCAL_ACCOUNT), of kind [`HARNESS_LOGIN`](crate::HARNESS_LOGIN): the program run on the configuration as it stands, nothing applied. A host lists it without anyone adding it, and `usage` and `models` answer for a grant of that kind. A provider that offers none refuses such a grant as a kind it does not list.

default.description: The URL used when the setting is absent.

inputs.description: The answers to the method's `inputs` schema.

state_dir.description: A private directory where the harness runs, made by the host, where the CLI runs and writes what it signs in with. The host removes it however the login ended.

timeout_ms.description: The most the whole login may take.

credentials.description: What the login wrote or was given, read from the files it wrote.

label.description: A name for people the provider learned (an email address), when it did.

expires_at.description: When the credentials stop working, as an RFC 3339 time, when known.

checked.description: Whether the provider verified the login with a call that spends nothing.

schema.description: A schema of the fields. A secret is a property marked `writeOnly` and `x-sensitive`, and the host answers it in [`LoginAnswer::secrets`].

values.description: The values of the fields that are not secrets, an object.

secrets.description: The values of the sensitive fields, by property name.

url.description: The page, as the CLI printed it.

user_code.description: The one-time code the person confirms there, when the CLI printed one.

expires_ms.description: How long the page and code stay good, in milliseconds, when known.

id.description: The host's id for the account: text the host assigns, 1 to [`ACCOUNT_ID_MAX`] bytes with no control character, opaque to the provider, echoed (into usage reports) and never interpreted.

settings.description: The kind's non-secret settings, an object its catalog schema accepts.

credentials.description: The kind's secrets, by the key path of the sensitive setting each fills.

state_dir.description: A private directory where the harness runs, made by the host, for a kind whose catalog entry says `state_dir`. The provider writes the account there and starts the harness on it.

revision.description: Counts the host's stored copies of the credentials, so a renewal says which it renews.

provides.description: The standards the account provides, from the catalog of whoever made it. A harness reads it only for a `kind` its own catalog does not list: it then applies the account as the first of its `accepts` that this names.

account.description: The account, with the credentials the host holds.

credentials.description: The credentials after the renewal, when it made new ones; absent when nothing changed.

expires_at.description: When the credentials now stop working, as an RFC 3339 time, when known.

not_renewed_because.description: Why nothing was renewed (not within the harness's renewal window, say), when so. It shows no credential.

from_revision.description: The revision of the grant the renewal replaces.

credentials.description: The credentials now, whole: every key of the grant.

expires_at.description: When they stop working, as an RFC 3339 time, when known.

sequence.description: Counts what happened to this account, renewals and losses together, from 1, without a gap or a repeat for as long as the provider lives, so the host orders chained rotations by it. The same event reaches every keeper that is live for the account and carries the same sequence: the host deduplicates by (account, sequence).

reason.description: Why, for people; it shows no credential.

sequence.description: As [`AccountRenewal::sequence`]: one count for the account's renewals and losses.

environment.description: Variables for what the provider runs or reaches to ask (a proxy, say), over its configuration's. A provider shows none of them in an answer, a refusal, an error or a log.

supported.description: Whether the account's provider reports usage for it at all.

x-enum-labels.inferred: Read from an error's words, a 429 or a refusal, by the provider or the host. The bucket's `evidence` holds the words, for logs; nothing parses it.

sources.description: Which kinds of figure it can give at all.

account.description: The host's id for the account, echoed and never interpreted.

revision.description: Grows by one with each change the provider instance sees of the account, so a reader that polls keeps the newest and an unchanged account costs nothing.

observed_at.description: The newest bucket's `observed_at`, in Unix seconds; `0` with no bucket.

label.description: What a person sees, when the harness has a name apart from the id.

oneOf.description: The harness did not say. A reader counts it as covering every model, so an exhausted bucket of unknown coverage stops the account for each of them.
These models only, by the ids or aliases `models()` lists.
A coverage a newer writer named; a reader treats it as unknown.

x-enum-labels.permille: A percentage only, when the provider gives no absolute number: `limit` is 1000 and `used` thousandths, so the arithmetic is the same for every unit.

used.description: How much is used, when the harness said.

limit.description: How much the bucket holds, when the harness said.

remaining.description: How much is left, when the harness said.

oneOf.description: All at once when the window ends, such as a five-hour or weekly allowance.

length.description: How long the window is, when the harness says.

resets_at.description: When it ends, in Unix seconds, when the harness says.

oneOf.description: A refill a newer writer named; a reader treats it as unknown.

x-enum-labels.warning: The harness said it is nearly used. Only when the harness said so: a host applies its own thresholds to the bucket's fraction.
x-enum-labels.exhausted: Nothing is left until the bucket refills.

status.description: What the harness says of it.

observed_at.description: When these figures were read, in Unix seconds.

known.description: Whether the provider listed them; when not, `models` is empty.

unknown_because.description: Why it could not, when `known` is false.

x-enum-labels.not_installed: The program the account's models are asked of is not on the machine.
x-enum-labels.failed: The program is there and could not be asked; the text says what.

unknown_kind.description: What kind of reason that is, when the program could not be started; absent when it simply lists its models only once a session has started.

signed_out.description: Whether the program, though it listed its models, says nobody is signed in, so a session on the machine's own login would be refused its first prompt. Says nothing of an account a host applies.

id.description: The program's own identifier or alias for it.

name.description: What the program shows a person, when it has a name apart from the identifier; a provider that knows the version puts it here too.

description.description: The program's one-line description, when it gives one.

resolved.description: The model an alias or default resolves to, as the program names it.

version.description: The model and its version as a person reads them (`Opus 5.5`), when the program can say it.

efforts.description: The efforts this model takes, in the program's order; empty when it lists none for it.

default_effort.description: The effort the model uses when none is named, when the program says.

is_default.description: Whether the program uses this model when none is named.
